accessibility_source_findings.finding: After a successful Entregar, load() sets loading=true and ListState swaps the whole list for skeletons, unmounting the focused button; nothing restores focus (no .focus() call exists in frontend/src). Keyboard and screen-reader users are dropped to the document start on a page that can hold hundreds of cards.

Handoff success is not announced: the confirmation span has no live region and is keyed to status 'delivered', which the backend never returns (it returns pending_ack/partial/failed). Only errors use role=alert.
Every card repeats the same button name 'Entregar' and the same group legend 'Destinos' with no reference to the item title, so controls are indistinguishable in a controls list.

ConfidenceBadge maps medium->warning and low->caution, HandoffStatusBadge maps watching->warning, onto @pr-federation/react 0.3.0 tones that the repo's own audit records as failing contrast. The mapping is unchanged and the package pin is unchanged; the CSS values themselves are not in the snapshot.

Below the md breakpoint the Pipeline card grid has one implicit auto column; each card is a grid item with default min-width:auto containing a nowrap (truncate) title, so a long title can widen the track past the viewport.
Home renders a <main> inside the shell's <main>, giving two nested main landmarks.
No skip-to-content link; on narrow screens the brand plus 8 nav links precede the content on every page.
Program timeline search input has no accessible name other than its placeholder; the wrapping label contains only an icon.
Filter chips (Pipeline domains, timeline phases) and the theme button convey selection by colour/glyph only; no aria-pressed or aria-current.

Pages bypass the i18n helper: Handoff is hard-coded Spanish, PipelineItemDetail, WaterDisruption, ProgramTimeline and ErrorBoundary are hard-coded English, while html lang follows the toggle. Content language can disagree with the declared language.
Pipeline and PipelineItemDetail loading, empty and backend-unreachable messages are plain elements without role=status/alert, unlike the ListState pages.
Topbar buttons are 34px high, the shadcn Button default is h-9 (36px), and Pipeline chips use py-1 text-sm; all below a 44px target.
Signals table has no caption and th cells have no scope; its horizontal scroll container is not keyboard focusable.
Badge explanations (confidence band, evidence tier, routing target) are exposed only through title attributes.
Dispatch error text uses text-red-700 with no dark-mode variant.

special_adjudications.question: Shared warning/caution contrast: where defined, where used, ratio, and do the recorded failing values still exist?
special_adjudications.answer: Three colour sources exist. (1) --zip-warning / --zip-warning-foreground are defined as HSL in frontend/src/zip-design/tokens.css:47-48 (light) and :104-105 (dark) and are referenced nowhere else in frontend/src; there is no caution token in zip-design, index.css or tailwind.config.js. (2) The warning and caution tones actually rendered come from @pr-federation/react 0.3.0 via federationTone(): ConfidenceBadge medium->warning and low->caution (ConfidenceBadge.jsx:13,15), HandoffStatusBadge watching->warning (HandoffStatusBadge.jsx:19). Those badges render on Monitor/Signals/MatterDetail/EntityDetail via SignalCard.jsx:39,41, Matters.jsx:64-65, MatterDetail.jsx:68-69, SignalsTable.jsx:98-99, Pipeline.jsx:62, PipelineItemDetail.jsx:96, Handoff.jsx:97. (3) Amber Tailwind classes are used for the BLOCKED phase badge (ProgramTimeline.jsx:14) and the Geo/Geology domain badge (DomainBadge.jsx:11). No contrast ratio is given: the snapshot contains no hex foreground/background pair for any of these (zip tokens are HSL and unused, Tailwind palette and the federation stylesheet are not in the snapshot; frontend/node_modules is absent). The recorded failure is docs/A11Y_AUDIT.md:36-45, citing --fd-st-warning-fg:#b45309 and --fd-st-caution-fg:#a16207 in node_modules/@pr-federation/react/dist/federation.css. Those values appear nowhere in the snapshot except that document, so their current existence cannot be confirmed or refuted from source. What is confirmed: the dependency is still pinned to 0.3.0 (frontend/package.json:21) and the local tone mappings are unchanged, so nothing in this repo has changed that would fix it.

special_adjudications.question: Pipeline page responsiveness at narrow widths; horizontal overflow risk?
special_adjudications.answer: Pipeline.jsx uses cards, not a table. Container 'max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 py-8 space-y-8' (:101); stats row 'flex flex-wrap gap-4' (:110); domain chips 'flex flex-wrap gap-2' (:129) so the 8 chips wrap rather than scroll; list 'grid gap-3 md:grid-cols-2' (:157), i.e. one column below Tailwind md (768px) and two above; badges 'flex flex-wrap' (:58). There is no overflow-x handling on the page. The shell collapses at 820px (AppShell.module.css:185-188) and sets min-width:0 on workspace/main (AppShell.module.css:113-115; adaptation.css:4-5). Overflow risk is present by source reading: below md the grid has a single implicit auto track and each card link is a grid item with 'block' but no min-w-0 (:49); the title inside is 'truncate' i.e. nowrap (:53) and the min-w-0 sits on an inner flex child (:52), which does not reduce the grid item's content-based minimum. A long title can therefore widen the track beyond the viewport; at md and above grid-cols-2 uses minmax(0,1fr) and the problem disappears. This matches the mobile-only overflow recorded in docs/A11Y_AUDIT.md:59-61, though that document attributes it to the chip bar, which does wrap. Not run, so this is an inference from CSS rules. PipelineItemDetail also has a 'grid grid-cols-2' metadata block with an unbroken monospace item_id (PipelineItemDetail.jsx:146-147) that can spill at narrow widths.

special_adjudications.question: Handoff page accessibility: labels, focus after submit, error announcement, button names, dry_run default
special_adjudications.answer: Labels: each checkbox is wrapped in a <label> with visible text (Handoff.jsx:106-111) inside a fieldset with legend 'Destinos' (:102-103); the legend is identical on every card and does not name the item. Focus management: none; after a successful send, load() flips loading and ListState replaces the list with skeletons, unmounting the focused button (Handoff.jsx:63, :29, :84; ListState.jsx:28-36). Error announcement: POST errors render in a span with role=alert (:131); there is no aria-live for success or partial messages (:132-133), and the success message is keyed to 'delivered', which the backend never returns (dispatch.py:259 returns pending_ack/partial/failed), so a successful send shows nothing. The list-load error branch (:31-33) is unreachable because getHandoffs returns [] on failure (pipelineClient.js:46). Loading is announced through ListState role=status (ListState.jsx:30). Button names: text 'Entregar' / 'Entregando…' (:129), not unique per item; disabled while sending or with no target selected (:127). dry_run: defaults to false on both sides. The client sends dry_run: Boolean(options.dryRun) (pipelineClient.js:63) and Handoff passes no options (Handoff.jsx:61); the backend model default is False (server/backend/main.py:148). There is no dry-run control and no confirmation step, so Entregar performs a live repository dispatch.

special_adjudications.question: Is frontend/src/components/Header.jsx dead code with its own nav list?
special_adjudications.answer: Yes. Nothing imports it: a grep for 'Header' across frontend/src, frontend/tests and frontend/index.html returns only its own export (Header.jsx:66) and a comment in i18n/en.js:6.
